about: MSFP Media version 0's video (spec/v0/video.md); sections named alone are video's: what a caller keeps of a video title (section 3.1), of its copies (sections 3.2 to 3.8), of an extra (section 3.9) and of a local title (section 3.10); what a caller reads from a codecs string (section 3.5); title keys of the tvdb and local schemes (sections 4.4 and 4.5); the video members of play's answer and the URLs built from its ticket (sections 5.3 and 6.1); the previews call (section 5.6); the fonts of a copy (section 6.6); subtitle parts and fonts as a caller checks them (sections 6.3 to 6.6). Generated by tools/vectors, which re-derives every output from its text; no implementation has produced them yet.

titles, extras, localTitles: text is one entry of a titles answer, as JSON; the caller asked for the libraries listed in libraries. A title has no kind: its key names it, and a kind member is ignored. valid false: the caller skips the title, for the reason given. valid true: output is what it keeps, members in this order: key, library, extraType, name, year, image, place (season, episode), with, ids (its members sorted), copies (each as in copies); absent members left out.

copies: text is one entry of a title's copies. valid false: the caller skips that copy alone. valid true: output is what it keeps, members in the order of the table of section 3.2 (id, edition, durationMs, startMs, endMs, mediaType, size, etag, parts, video, audioTracks, subtitleTracks, chapters, segments, previewLayout, threeD), streams and tracks in the order of the tables of sections 3.3, 3.4 and 5.5; absent members left out, audioTracks always written. The cap of 16 copies, repeated copy IDs and a title left without copies are in titles.

Open fields (the codecs, edition, role, subtitle format, objects, segment kind, extraType, hdr, threeD) keep any token of base section 3 (1 to 32 characters of a-z 0-9 . _ -), known or not, and mediaType any media type of base section 3 (lowercase, one /, each half starting with a letter or a digit, at most 127 characters of a-z 0-9 . + - _ /); a value that isn't well formed is dropped alone when optional, and a required one (mediaType, a video or audio codec, extraType) takes its copy, video, track or extra with it. colour members are H.273 code points, 0 to 255, 2 counting as absent.

codecs: text is a video stream or an audio track as kept (codec, codecs, bitDepth, dv). valid true: output is what the caller decides by: the parts of codecs it reads (profile, tier, level, chroma, constraints, mp4a, the part after mp4a for AAC), the parts it ignores left out (H.264 constraint flags, HEVC compatibility flags, VP9 level, AV1 colour), bitDepth from the stream's own field when it has one, else from codecs, and dolbyVision, the Dolby Vision string rebuilt from the base 4CC and dv. valid false: codecs missing or malformed where it is required (h264, hevc, av1, vp9, aac, dts), or unreadable for its codec: the caller treats the copy as one it can't play as it is.

answers: text is the video members of play's answer (subtitles, fontCount) with the playback's ticket, for the copy answerCopy (as kept), the source's stream root being streamRoot. valid true: output is what the caller keeps, and urls, every URL it may build from the ticket: each subtitle entry's (subtitles/, pictures/, ass/), fonts/0 to fontCount - 1, and the copy's sheets, trickplay/0 to the sheet count of its previewLayout - 1. valid false: it refuses the answer.

fontSets: text is the sizes in bytes of one copy's fonts. valid true: within the bounds of section 6.6, output their count and total; valid false: the first font that breaks a bound, which the source doesn't serve and a caller refuses.
localKeys, tvdbKeys: text is a title key. valid true: kind is the kind it names (movie, series, season, episode or extra); valid false: the receiver skips a title with that key.

previews: side request is a previews request as the source reads it: valid false means it answers 400 (the 404s depend on what it offers, not on the request). side answer is a previews answer as the caller reads it: valid false means it refuses the answer and fetches no sheet; valid true: output is the ticket and etag it keeps.

Tracks' languages are kept only as valid tags, in the form base section 2.4 sends them (a tag sentTag of base.json's languageCodes leaves unchanged), never converted; the conversions of base section 2.4 are in base.json (languageCodes).

webvtt: a part (text, or hex when it isn't UTF-8), whether it is refused, and the rebuilt part (output) when it isn't (section 6.3). The 5 MiB part and 16 MiB track sizes and the 50,000 and 200,000 cue counts are not exercised here.
ass: the same for ASS (section 6.4). The 5 MiB and 16 MiB sizes and the 50,000 and 200,000 event counts are not exercised here.
pgs: PGS parts, in hex, as section 6.5 checks them; times are zero. An empty part (no hex) is valid. The 64 MiB size and 20,000 objects are not exercised here.

fonts: tiny font headers, in hex (a table directory and 4 zero bytes per table, not real fonts), as section 6.6 checks them; type is the media type a valid font is relayed as. The 10 MiB size is not exercised here.
